evals.prompt: Hey, can you review the test quality of my project? Here are the test files and the output from running jest. I want to know how good my tests are according to Kent Beck's desiderata.
evals.expected_output: A terminal table scoring all 12 desiderata 1-5, a /60 total, and top-3 specific improvements referencing actual file/line issues in the provided Jest test files.
assertions: The output includes a table with all 12 desiderata scored
Each score is in the range 1-5
A /60 total score is shown
Top-3 improvements are listed with specific references to the provided files
The Isolated property scores 2 or lower (shared mutable testUser, beforeAll not reset per test)
The Fast property scores 2 or lower (17s suite with 4s+ real network calls per checkout test)
The Behavioral or Structure-insensitive property scores 2 or lower (spy on _fetchFromDb internal method)
Checkout network calls are flagged as a Fast improvement
The skill offers to save a markdown report

evals.prompt: I'm working on a Python service and want to audit my test suite. Can you check my tests against the 12 test desiderata and let me know where I stand? Here's the test file and the pytest output.
evals.expected_output: A scored table for all 12 desiderata, with the Fast property flagged clearly due to the 45s sleep, Deterministic flagged for time.sleep and wall-clock ordering, and top-3 improvements focused on those issues.
assertions: The output includes a table with all 12 desiderata scored
A /60 total score is shown
The Fast property scores 1 or 2 (47s suite, 45s sleep)
The Deterministic property scores 2 or lower (time.sleep and wall-clock test)
The Automated property scores 4 or 5 (GitHub Actions CI is present)
The sleep(2) call is specifically called out as a problem
Top-3 improvements are listed
The skill offers to save a markdown report

evals.prompt: we have a small auth module, here are the tests and the output. we run them manually with node auth.test.js. just curious how they hold up against Kent Beck's test desiderata
evals.expected_output: A scored table calling out the lack of a test framework, no CI, timing-dependent test, and no assertions framework. Automated scores low. Top-3 improvements include adopting a test runner and adding CI.
assertions: The output includes a table with all 12 desiderata scored
A /60 total score is shown
The Automated property scores 1 or 2 (manual run, no CI detected)
The Deterministic property scores 2 or lower (setTimeout-based timing test)
The Specific property scores 2 or lower (no test framework means failures give no location info)
Top-3 improvements are listed
Adopting a test runner (jest, vitest, mocha or similar) is recommended
The skill offers to save a markdown report
